arxiv-1612-02567.title: Order statistics of horse racing and the randomly broken stick
arxiv-1612-02567.creator: Peter A. Bebbington, Julius Bonart
arxiv-1612-02567.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Peter A. Bebbington, Julius Bonart. We find a remarkable agreement between the statistics of a randomly divided interval and the observed statistical patterns and distributions found in horse racing betting markets. We compare the distribution of implied winning odds, the average true winning probabilities, the implied odds conditional on a win, and the average implied odds of the winning horse with the corresponding quantities from the “randomly broken stick problem”. We observe that the market is at least to some degree informationally efficient.

arxiv-2102-07640.title: Real-time tracking of COVID-19 and coronavirus research updates through text mining
arxiv-2102-07640.creator: Yutong Jin, Jie Li, Xinyu Wang, Peiyao Li, Jinjiang Guo, Junfeng Wu, Dawei Leng, Lurong Pan*
arxiv-2102-07640.description: Abstract The novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) which causes COVID-19 is an ongoing pandemic. There are ongoing studies with up to hundreds of publications uploaded to databases daily. We are exploring the use-case of artificial intelligence and natural language processing in order to efficiently sort through these publications.

arxiv-2203-02616.title: Chance-Constrained Optimization in Contact-Rich Systems for Robust Manipulation
arxiv-2203-02616.creator: Yuki Shirai, Devesh K. Jha, Arvind U. Raghunathan, Diego Romeres
arxiv-2203-02616.description: Abstract This paper presents a chance-constrained formulation for robust trajectory optimization during manipulation. In particular, we present a chance-constrained optimization for Stochastic Discrete-time Linear Complementarity Systems (SDLCS). To solve the optimization problem, we formulate Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming with Chance Constraints (MIQPCC).

arxiv-2207-11821.title: Maximizing Entanglement Routing Rate in Quantum Networks: Approximation Algorithms
arxiv-2207-11821.creator: Tu N. Nguyen, Dung H. P. Nguyen, Dang H. Pham, Bing-Hong Liu, Hoa N. Nguyen
arxiv-2207-11821.description: Abstract There will be a fast-paced shift from conventional network systems to novel quantum networks that are supported by the quantum entanglement and teleportation, key technologies of the quantum era, to enable secured data transmissions in the next-generation of the Internet. Despite this prospect, migration to quantum networks cannot be done at once, especially on the aspect of quantum routing.

arxiv-2305-06620.title: Improving Continual Relation Extraction by Distinguishing Analogous Semantics
arxiv-2305-06620.creator: Wenzheng Zhao, Yuanning Cui, Wei Hu
arxiv-2305-06620.description: Abstract Continual relation extraction (RE) aims to learn constantly emerging relations while avoiding forgetting the learned relations. Existing works store a small number of typical samples to re-train the model for alleviating forgetting. However, repeatedly replaying these samples may cause the overfitting problem.

arxiv-2308-11012.title: On scattering problem off the potential, decreasing as inverse square of distance
arxiv-2308-11012.creator: V. A. Gradusov, S. L. Yakovlev
arxiv-2308-11012.description: Abstract A solution of the scattering problem is obtained for the Schrödinger equation with the potential of induced dipole interaction, which decreases as the inverse square of the distance. Such a potential arises in the collision of an incident charged particle with a complex of charged particles (for example, in the collision of electrons with atoms).

arxiv-2409-14480.title: Large-Time Asymptotics for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili I Equation
arxiv-2409-14480.creator: Samir Donmazov, Jiaqi Liu, Peter Perry
arxiv-2409-14480.description: Abstract . We prove large-time asymptotics for solutions of the KP I equation with small initial data. Our assumptions on the initial data rule out lump solutions but enable us to give a precise description of the radiation field at large times. Our analysis uses the inverse scattering method and involves large-time asymptotics for solutions to a non-local Riemann-Hilbert problem.

arxiv-2412-19577.title: Gauging or extending bulk and boundary conformal field theories: Application to bulk and domain wall problem in topological matter and their descriptions by (mock) modular covariant
arxiv-2412-19577.creator: Yoshiki Fukusumi
arxiv-2412-19577.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yoshiki Fukusumi. We formulate the Z N Z_{N} group gauging operations (or group extensions) in (smeared) boundary conformal field theories (BCFTs) and bulk conformal field theories, and study their applications to various phenomena in topologically ordered systems. We apply the resultant theories to analyze the correspondence between the renormalization group (RG) flow of CFTs and the classification of topological quantum field theories with the testable information of general classes of partition functions.

arxiv-2504-19825.title: Detailed Design and Optimization of Ferro-Electric Tuners
arxiv-2504-19825.creator: Ilan Ben-Zvi, Alick Macpherson, Samuel Smith
arxiv-2504-19825.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ilan Ben-Zvi, Alick Macpherson, Samuel Smith. A detailed, step-by-step design methodology of a Ferroelectric Fast Reactive Tuner (FE-FRT) capable of modulating Mega VAR reactive powers on a sub-microsecond time scale is given. Closed expressions of values for all the components of the tuner are detailed, and tuner performance optimization is addressed, resulting in a Figure of Merit measure of FE-FRT tuner performance and use case applicability over a wide range of RF frequencies and reactive power levels.

arxiv-2505-07614.title: Bant: Byzantine Antidote via Trial Function and Trust Scores
arxiv-2505-07614.creator: Gleb Molodtsov, Daniil Medyakov, Sergey Skorik, Nikolas Khachaturov, Shahane Tigranyan, Vladimir Aletov, Aram Avetisyan, Martin Takáč, Aleksandr Beznosikov
arxiv-2505-07614.description: Abstract Recent advancements in machine learning have improved performance while also increasing computational demands. While federated and distributed setups address these issues, their structures remain vulnerable to malicious influences. In this paper, we address a specific threat: Byzantine attacks, wherein compromised clients inject adversarial updates to derail global convergence.

arxiv-2508-10992.title: When higher-order interactions enhance synchronization: the case of the Kuramoto model
arxiv-2508-10992.creator: Riccardo Muolo, Hiroya Nakao, Marco Coraggio
arxiv-2508-10992.description: Abstract Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in complex systems, observed across a wide range of natural and engineered contexts. The Kuramoto model provides a foundational framework for understanding synchronization among coupled oscillators, traditionally assuming pairwise interactions. However, many real-world systems exhibit group and many-body interactions, which can be effectively modeled through hypergraphs.

arxiv-2509-14540.title: Design-Space Exploration of Distributed Neural Networks in Low-Power Wearable Nodes
arxiv-2509-14540.creator: Meghna Roy Chowdhury, Ming-Che Li, Archisman Ghosh
arxiv-2509-14540.description: Abstract Wearable devices are revolutionizing personal technology, but their usability is often hindered by frequent charging due to high power consumption. This paper introduces Distributed Neural Networks (DistNN), a framework that distributes neural network computations between resource-constrained wearable nodes and resource-rich hubs to reduce energy at the node without sacrificing performance.

pmc-10802774.title: Open-access publications: a double-edged sword for critical care researchers in lowand middle-income countries
pmc-10802774.creator: Antonio Paulo Nassar Jr, Flávia Ribeiro Machado, Felipe Dal-Pizzol, Jorge Ibrain Figueira Salluh
pmc-10802774.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Although the initial moves in this chess game were met with skepticism by both publishers and scientists alike, OA publishing quickly became a standard model that encompassed both new and traditional, nonindexed and high-impact journals. In critical care, 3 out of the top 10 impact factor journals exclusively dedicated to the field are OA, and most of the others have gradually adhered to a partial OA model (where the authors may opt-in to an OA publication).

pmc-11510397.title: DNA: Novel Crystallization Regulator for Solid Polymer Electrolytes in High-Performance Lithium-Ion Batteries
pmc-11510397.creator: Xiong Cheng, Joonho Bae, Henrich Frielinghaus
pmc-11510397.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In this work, we designed a novel polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)@DNA solid polymer electrolyte, wherein DNA, as a plasticizer-like additive, reduced the crystallinity of the solid polymer electrolyte and improved its ionic conductivity. At the same time, due to its Lewis acid effect, DNA promotes the dissociation of lithium salts when interacting with lithium salt anions and can also fix the anions, creating more free lithium ions in the electrolyte and thus improving its ionic conductivity.

pmc-12382603.title: The interaction of second trimester prenatal maternal inflammation and psychosocial stress on offspring depressive symptoms in adolescence
pmc-12382603.creator: Rachel H Furlan, Madeline R Pike, Emily Lipner, Elizabeth C Breen, Barbara A Cohn, Piera M Cirillo, Nickilou Y Krigbaum, Ann M Kring, Thomas M Olino, Lauren B Alloy, Lauren M Ellman

Similarly, interactions between sources of inflammation and maternal daily life stress in T2, previously have been associated with increased offspring adolescent depressive symptoms.

pmc-12627227.title: Automated Oxygen Delivery in Home Setting for Patients with COPD on Long-Term Oxygen Therapy – A Randomized Crossover Feasibility Trial
pmc-12627227.creator: Linette Marie Kofod, Ejvind Frausing Hansen, Morten Tange Kristensen, Barbara Cristina Brocki, Elisabeth Westerdahl
pmc-12627227.description: RationalePatients with COPD on long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) have an unmet need for oxygen adjustments during sleep, rest, and activity, documented by continuous monitoring of oxygen saturation (SpO2). While emerging technology enables automated adjustments, its feasibility in home settings remains uncertain. This randomized crossover trial evaluated the feasibility and preliminary effects of continuous automated oxygen titration at home.

pmc-12653967.title: Device-Based Therapies for Refractory Angina
pmc-12653967.creator: Andrea Caffè, Rocco A. Montone
pmc-12653967.description: A substantial proportion of patients with ischemic heart disease continue to experience recurrent or persistent angina despite optimized medical therapy and prior revascularization, highlighting the need for novel and effective treatment strategies. Device-based therapies have emerged as promising options to address this unmet clinical need.

pmc-12660860.creator: Khalil Choucair, Hafsa Imtiaz, Md Hafiz Uddin, Misako Nagasaka, Mohammad Najeeb Al-Hallak, Philip A Philip, Bassel El-Rayes, Boris C Pasche, Asfar S Azmi

pmc-13637159.title: Increased awareness around an ultra-rare disease can improve diagnosis delays: the French example in primary hyperoxalurias
pmc-13637159.creator: Lara Cabezas, Aurélie De Mul, Laurence Derain, Romain Pszczolinski, Cindy Castrale, Emmanuel Letavernier, Laurent Mesnard, Dominique Guerrot, Lise Allard, Olivia Boyer, Mélissa Ould Rabah, Isabelle Vrillion, François Nobili, Ariane Zaloszyc, Cécile Acquaviva, Justine Bacchetta, Sandrine Lemoine
pmc-13637159.description: BackgroundPrimary hyperoxalurias (PH) are rare recessive autosomal genetic diseases inducing increased hepatic oxalate production. Apart from genetic background, their prognosis depends mainly on diagnosis delay. We recently reported shorter diagnosis delay in children compared with adults (1.2 (0.1–3.0) versus 30 (17–36) years) in a French PH cohort of 52 patients diagnosed between 2015 and 2019.
